evidence.quote: Fourier Intelligence was founded in 2015 and is headquartered in Shanghai’s Zhangjiang Hi-Tech Park. Its core rehabilitation products are deployed in over 2,000 institutions across more than 40 countries.

Fourier’s march toward full-stack humanoid robotics began with its lower-limb exoskeleton in 2017, followed by the GR-1 humanoid in 2023, which became China’s first humanoid robot to reach mass production. In 2024, the company released GR-2. Cumulative funding tops $210M.

GR-3 stands 165 cm tall, weighs 71 kg, and has 55 degrees of freedom. It features an innovative soft-shell exterior with automotive-grade upholstery and 31 distributed pressure sensors for safe physical interaction with people.

Designed not just for functionality but for emotional connection, GR-3 is guided by the philosophy "Love, above all functionality." Its Full-Perception Multimodal Interaction System fuses vision, audio, and tactile feedback into a real-time emotional processing engine. GR-3 is expected to be deployed in nursing homes and rehabilitation centers.

Fourier’s approach emphasizes gamification and patient engagement, with the ExoMotion system connecting to interactive games and virtual environments that make repetitive therapy exercises more engaging and motivating for patients.

A systematic review and meta-analysis of thirteen randomized controlled trials published between 2015 and 2025 involving 424 post-stroke patients found that robotic therapy showed a moderate but statistically significant effect over conventional rehabilitation. Subgroup analysis revealed the strongest effects during the subacute phase and acute phase, while the chronic phase yielded limited improvement.

Fourier’s Series E funding round secured nearly ¥800 million (about $109.1 million). Fourier plans to use the funding to achieve its product goal of creating the best embodied AI entity and to advance its vision of empowering human life with robotics technology.
